T1.question: one drop, varied cadence AND distance back: what bounds the reversal window
T1.note: BOTH. At 10s and 60s the cut sits between 16 and 25 SAMPLES, identical in sample terms across a sixfold change in elapsed time; at 600s it is already quiet at 10 back, which 60s at 16 back is not. So a sample count and a duration each bound it and the shorter one bites. A scheduled shift reset is hours old and outside the duration bound at any cadence, so it cannot reach this arm -- a bridge withholding history to protect it is protecting nothing.

M3.note: BRIDGES states the count-inside-a-window trap for insufficient_samples only. It applies to every count-based tolerance, and this is one: a 50-sample corpus with reversals spread through it fires at six, and with the same six at the end fires at three. Neither number is the tolerance; the window is doing the work

K7.question: is the threshold ABSOLUTE or RELATIVE, and where is it
K7.note: if the same fraction fires at both scales, the threshold is relative -- which means a lifetime counter's balance is judged against a lifetime total. A real loss of forty parts against nine thousand is 0.45 %, and gets quieter every shift. The remedy is the bridge's: balance the derived per-interval rate, not the counter
